backlog.spec: Ramp Muon's momentum from 0.85 at step 0 linearly up to 0.95 over the first ~300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. If the script already has a momentum schedule, keep its endpoints and only change the ramp length. Do not change MATRIX_LR or any other hyperparameter.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Exclude the token embedding, lm_head, and all norm/scalar parameters from decoupled weight decay. Apply WEIGHT_DECAY only to the Muon matrix parameters, as now. Implement by setting weight_decay=0 in the Adam parameter groups.
backlog.title: Zero weight decay on embeddings and norms

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations in Muon from 5 to 3. This cuts optimizer overhead so more steps fit in the 300 s budget. Keep the same coefficients for the iteration you keep, and leave all LRs unchanged.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and leave every other learning rate unchanged. The current value is very aggressive for Adam on embeddings, so this tests whether a smaller step size on the input table improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: Lower embedding LR

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 while keeping the same warmdown schedule. Muon with orthogonalized updates often tolerates larger LRs, so this probes whether the current value is under-tuned for this short run.
backlog.title: Higher Muon matrix LR

backlog.spec: Multiply the Adam learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, SCALAR_LR) by (256 / model_dim) so they transfer across ASPECT_RATIO and DEPTH changes. Keep MATRIX_LR as-is. This is a muP-style correction that makes LR choices less brittle when the architecture changes.
backlog.title: Scale Adam LRs by model width

backlog.spec: After backward and before optimizer.step(), clip the global gradient norm of all trainable parameters to 1.0 using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_. This guards against occasional loss spikes at the high LRs used here.
backlog.title: Gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam optimizer for the token embedding parameters with Lion (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99, sign-based update), using an LR about 3x smaller than EMBEDDING_LR (roughly 0.1-0.2). Keep Adam for the other non-matrix groups and Muon for the matrices.
backlog.title: Lion for embedding table

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget. The LR still ends at FINAL_LR_FRAC. This shifts more of the run into the low-LR regime that usually gives the best final loss.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown ratio

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2% of the time budget before the existing schedule takes over. This avoids instability from the very large initial LRs on the embedding and scalar groups.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the LR decays to 10% of its peak instead of 0 at the end of the time budget. This tests whether a small residual LR helps the last few steps when the schedule is time-based.
backlog.title: Non-zero final LR fraction

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine curve over the warmdown window, going from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC times the peak. Use lr_mult = final + 0.5*(1-final)*(1+cos(pi*t)) with t from 0 to 1 across the warmdown. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown shape

backlog.spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. At a fixed 300 s budget this doubles the number of updates, which often helps small models that are not compute-bound. Adjust gradient accumulation so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE stays 64.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch for more steps

backlog.spec: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 by increasing gradient accumulation steps, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64. Each step averages more tokens, which can give smoother gradients for Muon at the cost of fewer updates. Re-check that the time budget still fits.
backlog.title: Larger total batch

backlog.spec: Train with a shorter context for the first 30% of the time budget (for example half the sequence length, with the batch reshaped to keep the same token count per step), then switch to full context. Shorter sequences early give cheaper steps and faster initial loss reduction. Implement by reshaping the existing batch tensors without touching the data loader or the eval path.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'LLLL' so every layer uses full context. At this sequence length the sliding windows may save little time while removing some context, so this checks whether full attention improves the bits-per-byte score per token.
backlog.title: Full attention window pattern

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and keep ASPECT_RATIO at 64 so model_dim becomes 384, then keep HEAD_DIM at 128 so there are 3 heads. Fewer layers run faster per step, which may help within the 300 s limit. Confirm the window pattern length still matches the depth.
backlog.title: Shallower and wider model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and reduce ASPECT_RATIO to 48 so model_dim is about 480, rounding it to a multiple of HEAD_DIM. More layers can improve quality per parameter at similar cost. Confirm WINDOW_PATTERN still applies cleanly to the new depth.
backlog.title: Deeper and narrower model

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so there are twice as many attention heads at the same model width. More heads with smaller dimension is a common choice for small models and may improve the attention patterns learned in a short run.
backlog.title: Smaller head dimension

backlog.spec: Use the squared ReLU activation, relu(x)**2, in the MLP block in place of the current nonlinearity. Keep the MLP hidden width unchanged. This is a cheap change that often improves loss per FLOP in small GPTs.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU MLP activation

backlog.spec: Add a learned per-layer scalar that mixes the normalized token embedding x0 back into the residual stream before every block, initialized to 0. Keep the existing residual path otherwise unchanged. This gives deep layers direct access to the raw token signal, which helps byte-level prediction.
backlog.title: Learned skip from input embedding

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block to compute attention and MLP from the same normalized input and add both to the residual, instead of applying them sequentially. This reduces the critical path per layer and can speed up each step under torch.compile.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block to zero, while keeping the other weights at their current init. Zero-init residual branches make the early network close to identity and often stabilize short training runs.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized output projections

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits, dim=-1)**2) to the training loss to keep output logits from drifting in scale. Apply only in the training loss, leaving the evaluation computation unchanged. This is a small, cheap regularizer for the lm_head.
backlog.title: Logit z-loss regularizer

backlog.spec: Add dropout with probability 0.05 on the outputs of attention and MLP before they are added to the residual stream. Keep it disabled at evaluation time through the usual model.eval() mode. Only do this if the model is not already severely under-fit; it is a probe of mild regularization.
backlog.title: Dropout in the residual branches

backlog.spec: Maintain an EMA copy of the trainable parameters with decay 0.999 updated after every optimizer step. Before the final training step ends, copy the EMA weights into the live model parameters so the harness evaluates the averaged model. Do not change the evaluation call itself.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights

backlog.spec: Change the torch.compile call to use mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' or dynamic=False, whichever gives higher steps per second on the A100 in a quick check. The goal is more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s window without changing the model math.
backlog.title: Compile mode tuning

backlog.spec: Set the beta1 for the scalar/per-layer parameter group to 0.9 and keep 0.95 for beta2, leaving the embedding and lm_head groups at ADAM_BETAS as now. Higher momentum on the small scalar parameters can smooth their updates over the many steps in the run.
backlog.title: Use Adam beta1 0.9 for scalars

backlog.spec: Initialize the lm_head weight with a std of about 1/sqrt(model_dim) scaled by 0.5 instead of the current init, keeping UNEMBEDDING_LR unchanged. A smaller initial output scale typically reduces the early loss spike and speeds initial learning.
backlog.title: Untied lm_head initialization scale

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon LR for each transformer block by a factor that decreases linearly with depth, from 1.0 at the first layer to 0.6 at the last. Deeper layers get smaller updates, which can stabilize training across the 8 or more blocks. Implement by grouping the matrix parameters per layer.
backlog.title: Per-layer learning-rate decay

backlog.spec: Start training with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 for the first 30% of the 300 s time budget, then switch to 2**19 for the remainder. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and sequence length unchanged, and recompute gradient accumulation steps from the current total batch each time it changes (the gradient-accumulation loop already exists, so only the target count varies). Scale the LR schedule position by elapsed time as before and leave Muon and Adam LRs unchanged. The goal is more optimizer steps early, when loss drops fastest, without giving up the larger batch later.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp from 2^18 to 2^19 tokens

backlog.spec: In every attention layer, apply rotary position embedding only to the first half of each head's query and key dimensions. The second half stays unrotated (NoPE), so those dimensions carry content-only matching. Keep HEAD_DIM, the number of heads, the sliding-window pattern and all other code unchanged. This is a small change to the RoPE helper and its call site, and it adds no parameters.
backlog.title: Partial RoPE: leave half of each head's dimensions position-free

backlog.spec: After scaled-dot-product attention, multiply each head's output by a learned sigmoid gate computed from the layer's normalized input, g = sigmoid(x @ W_g) with W_g a new Linear(model_dim, n_heads) initialized to zero so the gate starts at 0.5. Apply the gate per head before the output projection. This adds a small number of parameters per layer and gives the model a learned way to suppress or pass each head, as in recent gated-attention work. Do not change the optimizer grouping beyond placing W_g with the other matrix parameters for Muon.
backlog.title: Sigmoid output gate per attention head

backlog.spec: Keep the value projection output from layer 0 and add a scaled copy of it to the value vectors of every later attention layer, v_l = v_l + lambda_l * v_0, where lambda_l is a learnable scalar per layer initialized to 0.1 and optimized with the existing scalar-parameter Adam group. The first layer is unchanged. This lets deeper layers reuse early token-identity information with almost no extra compute. Make sure the cached value tensor is detached or kept in the graph consistently with the compiled forward pass.
backlog.title: Value-embedding residual from the first layer

backlog.spec: Scale the output of every attention and MLP residual branch by 1/sqrt(2 * DEPTH) at initialization, by multiplying the output of each output projection (c_proj for attention and MLP) by that constant. Leave the optimizer groups and LRs unchanged, and keep the zero-initialization that already exists for output projections if present. The aim is to keep the residual stream variance stable as depth grows, which can allow a higher effective learning rate for the matrix parameters. Only the init scale changes; the forward pass is unchanged.
backlog.title: DeepNet-style residual branch scaling

backlog.spec: During training, drop each transformer block's residual contribution (attention and MLP branches together) independently per sample with probability p_l = 0.1 * (l / (DEPTH - 1)), so the first layer is never dropped and the last drops at most 0.1. Rescale surviving branch outputs by 1/(1 - p_l) so the expected value matches. Disable dropping at evaluation time. Use a per-batch Bernoulli draw for simplicity. This regularizes a model that is still under-trained, so keep the probability ramp small.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth on residual blocks, ramped to 0.1

backlog.spec: In the training cross-entropy only, replace the target distribution with (1 - 0.02) on the true token and 0.02 / (V - 1) spread over the other vocabulary entries, using the built-in label_smoothing argument of F.cross_entropy. Do not change the validation loss or the evaluation path. Label smoothing usually costs a little likelihood, so this is a deliberately bold test of whether reduced overconfidence helps generalization in a single 300 s pass.
backlog.title: Label smoothing of 0.02 on the training loss

backlog.spec: Before the cross-entropy, replace the raw logits z with 15 * tanh(z / 15), so logits are smoothly bounded at plus or minus 15. Apply the cap only in the training forward pass and in the model's logit output used for evaluation, keeping the same function in both so the metric is computed consistently. If the model already applies a softcap, change its constant to 10 instead and report that the baseline already has one. The goal is to stabilize the Muon-trained lm_head early in the high-LR phase.
backlog.title: Tanh soft-cap on output logits

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1/sqrt(head_dim) attention scale with a learnable per-head scalar s_h initialized so that the effective scale equals the current fixed value, that is s_h = 1 at init, multiplied into the query-key product. Add the scalars to the existing scalar Adam group so they share its learning rate, and clamp them to the range [0.5, 2] times their initial value for stability. This lets each head choose its own sharpness with only n_heads extra parameters per layer. Attention outputs with the flash or SDPA kernel should be preserved by folding the scale into q before the kernel call.
backlog.title: Learnable per-head attention temperature

backlog.spec: Make the Muon weight decay coefficient a function of training progress: start at the current WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 and linearly anneal it to 0.0 over the time budget, updating it from the same elapsed-time fraction that drives the LR schedule. Apply the schedule only to the Muon matrix group. Adam groups keep their current settings. The idea is to regularize early, when the weights are still moving, and let the model fit more sharply during the final warmdown.
backlog.title: Decoupled weight decay that decays linearly to zero

backlog.spec: In the attention module, keep n_head query heads but reduce the key and value projections to 2 KV heads (n_kv_head = 2). Repeat each KV head across its group of query heads before the attention call, or use the flash attention GQA path if available. Size the c_k and c_v Linear layers to n_kv_head * head_dim outputs. Leave the rotary embedding, QK handling, sliding-window pattern, and everything else unchanged. The goal is fewer attention parameters and less memory traffic, so each step runs faster and more steps fit in the 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with 2 KV heads

backlog.spec: Keep DEPTH = 8 as the number of effective layers, but only instantiate 4 distinct transformer blocks. Layer i uses block i // 2, so each block is applied twice in sequence. Keep the per-layer scalars and the window pattern indexed by effective layer, not block. Use the same model_dim as before, which makes the model roughly half the parameter count. Optionally widen model_dim by about 1.4x to use the freed parameter budget, but only if the baseline throughput stays similar. This tests whether effective depth at lower parameter cost beats the current configuration.
backlog.title: ALBERT-style cross-layer weight sharing in pairs

backlog.spec: Add one learnable key vector and one learnable value vector per layer, of shape (n_kv_heads, head_dim), and prepend them as an extra key and value position in every attention call, so each query can attend to a sink with no positional encoding. Initialize the sink keys to zero and the sink values to zero. Do not count the sink position in the loss or the token count. Keep the sliding-window mask valid by letting the sink position always be visible to every query. This is a small change that may stabilize attention in short training runs.
backlog.title: Learnable attention-sink token (prepended key/value)

backlog.spec: Currently the token embedding and lm_head use Adam. Move the lm_head weight, and optionally the token embedding, into the Muon group, using the same Newton-Schulz orthogonalized update and the same momentum as the matrix parameters. Use a separate learning rate for these two matrices, starting at about 0.02 for the lm_head and keeping the embedding on Adam unless this is clearly better. Apply the existing weight decay convention to these matrices. Leave all other parameters unchanged. This tests whether orthogonalized updates help the large vocabulary-shaped matrices.
backlog.title: Orthogonalized (Muon-style) updates for embedding and lm_head

backlog.spec: Keep the existing Muon and Adam optimizers as the fast optimizers. Maintain a copy of the slow weights for all trainable parameters, initialized to the starting weights. Every k = 5 optimizer steps, update slow = slow + alpha * (fast - slow) with alpha = 0.5, then copy slow back into the fast weights. Run the slow-weight update under torch.no_grad(). Before evaluation, load the slow weights into the model, because the final model should be the slow one. Keep the time-based LR schedule as is. This is a bold change that trades a small amount of step efficiency for smoother convergence.
backlog.title: Lookahead wrapper around the base optimizer

backlog.spec: Add one extra small head that predicts the token two positions ahead, for example a Linear(model_dim, vocab) that shares the lm_head weight or is a separate zero-initialized projection. In the training loss, add lambda = 0.3 times the cross-entropy of this t+2 head against the targets shifted by two, masking the final two positions. Keep the main next-token loss as the primary objective. Use the same forward pass for both heads. At evaluation time use only the standard next-token head, so the harness-computed val_bpb is unaffected. This is a bold auxiliary-objective change that may give the trunk more signal per token.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head

backlog.spec: The metric is bits per byte, but the training loss averages cross-entropy per token, so multi-byte tokens are under-weighted relative to the metric. Compute a per-token byte length for each target id using only the tokenizer object that is exposed through the names train.py already imports from prepare.py, for example by decoding each id and taking the UTF-8 byte length, and build a lookup tensor on the GPU. Weight each token's cross-entropy by its byte length, and normalize by the sum of byte lengths in the batch instead of the token count. Do not reference any file paths or internals of prepare.py beyond the imported names. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy to match the bits-per-byte metric

backlog.spec: Since TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE was halved from 2^18 to 2^17, the matrix and embedding learning rates were tuned for the larger batch. Add a scale factor s = sqrt(TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE / 2**18) and multiply MATRIX_LR, EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, and SCALAR_LR by s, so the scale is about 0.71 at the current batch size. Compute s once from the constants at the top of train.py and apply it where the optimizer parameter groups are built. Keep the Adam betas, weight decay, and schedule unchanged. This is a cheap, principled test of whether the learning rates should be lowered with the smaller batch.
backlog.title: Batch-scaled learning rates for the halved batch

backlog.spec: During training only, randomly replace each input token id with a uniformly random token id with probability p = 0.05 before the embedding lookup. Do this on the input side only, and keep the targets unchanged so the model must predict the true next token from a corrupted context. Use a torch.rand mask of shape (B, T) and torch.randint for the replacements, and guard the entire branch with `if self.training`. At evaluation time, no tokens are corrupted. This is a small regularizer that may reduce overfitting, but since training is short it may also hurt, so the run tests the sign of the effect.
backlog.title: Token-embedding input dropout

backlog.spec: Keep the time-based linear warmdown structure, but add one warm restart. At time fraction 0.5 of the 300 s budget, jump the LR multiplier back up to 1.0 and decay it linearly to the final fraction by the end of the budget, using the same time-based progress for the whole remaining run. Concretely, compute progress over the budget with a sawtooth: phase = (t / budget) * 2 mod 1, so the multiplier is 1 - phase times the existing warmdown shape, with the final 0.1 of the budget at the existing final LR fraction. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups. This is a bold schedule test that may help escape a sharp minimum found in the first half.
backlog.title: One warm restart in the middle of the schedule

incumbent.description: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to double the number of optimizer steps, increasing updates on the small model within the 300s budget.

memo:
Incumbent is slot 8 (official 1.0942), reached by halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (-0.0203). More optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s is the only thing that has helped clearly. Larger batch (+0.0757) and DEPTH 10 (+0.0188) hurt badly. Schedule-shape changes (cosine warmdown +0.0101, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 +0.0033), LLLL windows (+0.0012), MATRIX_LR 0.06 (+0.0004), the attention output gate (+0.0052) and the EMA (+0.5696) did not help.

Small gains with 1 run each, possibly noise: WARMUP_RATIO 0.02 (-0.0011), half-length sequences (-0.0008), max-autotune (-0.0020). These were measured against different baselines, so some are not directly comparable.

Next: halve the batch again. Try a smaller model for more steps. Combine warmup 0.02, max-autotune and half-length sequences on the new batch, and replicate to check noise. Avoid schedule-shape and window changes. Check each edit applies and is not a no-op.
